header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #130 phase 3: reconcile subscription charges against real activity. Read issue #130 and closed issue #166 (phase 2, shipped in PR #169) first; the subscription model (terms, cancel/resume, extra charges, merchant link, EveryNMonths cadence, CardAutoCharge) already exists under server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/{actions/subscriptions,repositories}, controllers/SubscriptionsController.scala, lib/api/shared, and web/.../pages/subscriptions. The repo is PUBLIC: no PII anywhere (no real names, amounts, account digits) in code, tests, commits, PR text.

## Decisions already made (do not revisit)
1. Build ONE shared, pure, unit-testable date+amount matcher (a small service/object, no DB or HTTP inside) that scores/selects candidates by amount within a range, date within a tolerance window, and an optional merchant hint. Design it generically (candidate = date, amount, optional merchantId, id) so row-to-receipt matching can reuse it later, but only wire it to subscriptions now.
2. Tolerance window is a single server config value (see SubscriptionsConfig.scala for how config is done; default 5 days either side of the due date), not per subscription.
3. Reconciliation is DERIVED ON READ, not stored: for each subscription, expand the due dates inside the term(s) covering them (reuse the existing cadence/due-date logic; no drift for Monthly/Yearly/EveryNMonths; skip gaps between terms, so cancelled periods are never flagged), and match each due date against the user's expenses and bank statement rows. Per cycle status: Matched (with the matched expense/row id and actual date, flagged Late when outside the due date but inside tolerance), Retried (more than one matching charge attempt in the window), Missing (due date + tolerance passed with no match), Upcoming. Tie-break between two subscriptions with the same amount: prefer the one whose merchant matches the candidate, then the closest date; one charge may satisfy only one cycle (no double use).
4. The only persisted state is a manual payment log, for cash/portal/manual-transfer subscriptions that never produce a bank row: new table (next evolution number after the latest in the evolutions dir, follow existing evolution conventions, no DB CHECK constraints, FK to subscription ON DELETE CASCADE, user_id column) with subscription id, paid date, amount, optional note. A manual payment satisfies the cycle it falls in and counts as Matched.
5. Out of scope: term suggestions, receipt matching, any change to the existing subscription create/update behaviour.

## Deliverables
- Server: matcher; reconciliation action (get reconciliation for the user's subscriptions, optional single subscription); actions to add and delete a manual payment; repository/DAO for the log. Every query (read and write) has WHERE user_id = ?, every list query has ORDER BY, multi-step writes in a transaction. Limits: max 500 manual payments per subscription, note max 255 chars, amount positive and bounded like other subscription amounts. Validation at app level via the existing validated primitives (lib/common models, `.trusted` only in tests and DAO row parsing).
- Tapir endpoints in lib/api/shared, wired in ApiRouter and a controller; controller tests cover auth and encoding only, behaviour is tested in action integration tests using the real Postgres PostgresSpec pattern with random globally-unique data and no external calls. Matcher gets thorough pure unit tests (window edges, late, retried, missing, same-amount collision, gaps between terms, no double use, EveryNMonths and yearly cadence).
- MCP: extend the read-only subscriptions MCP surface (McpTools/McpDispatcher) with a `subscription_reconciliation` read tool returning the per-cycle statuses.
- Web: show per-subscription reconciliation on the existing SubscriptionsPage (missing / late / retried cycles clearly visible, matched ones collapsed), and a validated form to log/delete a manual payment. Every web form field must be a FormField over a validated primitive (see .orca/reviewers/frontend.md; mirror the existing Subscription*FormData and ui/forms primitives, extend ExpLocalDate/PositiveBigDecimal usage, no raw strings). No new route is needed; keep it reachable from the subscriptions page.
- Run scalafmtAll and scalafmtSbt, add specs, satisfy all .orca/reviewers gates. Commit per logical piece and open a PR.
